north_arrow_measurement.description: Ruled meridian line about 580 px long from S to a half-arrowhead at N, crossed by a compass circle with W and E; the label is lettered along the line. We fitted the two stretches of the shaft that are free of lettering and of the arrowhead.

rendering_check.note: Page skew and distortion checked on the printed 50-foot site grid: straight pieces of the horizontal grid lines, 370 px long, are rotated between -0.65 and +0.48 deg (SD 0.38 deg), and the vertical grid lines fan by up to 0.37 deg between the left and right margins (keystone of about 1 percent). We take 0.4 deg as the local rotation uncertainty of the reproduction.

sources.notes: The plan is printed rotated on the page; the drafted 50-foot grid is set square to the page, not to north.

main_system_reason: It contains the longest measured line, the street drain, and the walls that line the main street through the excavated part of Mound II, which is the layout the rest of the excavated buildings follow most closely.
notes: We measured Mackay's plan of the Harappa II level of Mound II (Plate IV), the only one of his four plans with a dense excavated street layout. Its north arrow is a ruled magnetic meridian dated 2 November 1935, so every bearing here is relative to magnetic north of that date and is not corrected for declination. The plan is printed turned on the page and its 50-foot site grid is square to the page, not to north. Each line was picked by hand on a 300 dpi render of the 300 dpi scan and fitted to the drawn ink within a narrow band; the street drain and the walls along the main street form the most coherent group, while the block south-west of the street, the north end of the street and the north-east corner each run a few degrees differently, so we report them as separate systems. The north-east corner walls are short and drawn as tapering masses, and their two lines are not at right angles to each other, so that system is weak. Lines are short (4 to 24 m) because the excavated area is small. Plates II (Mound I) and III (upper level of Mound II) were not measured.
